title: Impulse and Frequency Response Analyzer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Signals and Systems
Impulse Response
Step Response
Frequency Response
LTI Systems
description: Shows the impulse response, step response, magnitude response and phase response of five LTI systems (Butterworth low-pass and high-pass filters, differentiator, integrator and second-order resonant system) side by side, with linked cursors and sliders for cutoff frequency, filter order and damping ratio.

educational.topic: Impulse response, step response and frequency response of LTI systems
learningObjectives: Explain why the impulse response completely characterizes an LTI system
Relate the step response to the impulse response through integration
Connect features of the impulse response to features of the frequency response
Compare how low-pass, high-pass, differentiating, integrating and resonant systems change a signal in time and in frequency
prerequisites: Unit impulse and unit step functions

controls.label: Hover over a plot to move the time or frequency cursor

equations: s(t) = integral of h from -infinity to t
H(f) = integral of h(t) exp(-j 2 pi f t) dt
Resonant: H(s) = wn^2 / (s^2 + 2 zeta wn s + wn^2)
assumptions: All responses are closed-form; impulses and doublets are drawn as arrows
Pulse and square-wave outputs are built by superposing shifted step responses

keyQuestions: How does raising the cutoff frequency change the width of the impulse response?
What does a sharper cutoff cost in the step response?
How is ringing in the time domain related to a resonant peak in the frequency domain?
commonMisconceptions: The impulse response and the frequency response describe different aspects of a system rather than the same system
A higher filter order only changes the frequency response
A system with a wide bandwidth responds slowly
assessmentOpportunities: Read the time constant from the step response and the cutoff from the magnitude response and check that tau = 1/(2 pi fc)
Predict the pulse response from the step response
